policy: introduces denotes an original contribution to the literature, never first appearance in our database or an exposition/new proof of an existing object/result.

sources.title: The quantum G₂ link invariant
sources.coverage: Theorem 1.1 and §§1–2: original trivalent-graph calculus and its reduced boundary diagrams. Publication 1994; inspected arXiv v1 is dated October 7, 1991.
sources.summary: Kuperberg’s earlier construction of the G₂ link invariant and trivalent-graph calculus.
sources.dependency_review: Original-source attribution and learning reference. A strict unique-source dependency has not been established.

artifacts.note: Selected primary-source passages checked for origin attribution; no complete source ingestion is claimed.

introductions.introduction_evidence: The original work constructs the G₂ calculus on trivalent graphs (called freeways), with the G₂ local relations and boundary diagrams. Morrison 2011 §1 explicitly recalls Kuperberg 1994/1996; it does not introduce these graphs.
introductions.note: The later web/spider terminology packages this earlier graphical construction.

introductions.locator: §2, reduction of freeways and boundary spanning diagrams
introductions.introduction_evidence: The earlier G₂ graph calculus reduces faces of sizes at most five and uses the remaining boundary diagrams; Kuperberg 1996 §4 formulates these as non-elliptic webs. This credits the earlier construction, not the later choice of terminology.

The introduction announces the combinatorial rank-two spiders; §§3–4 give the spider formalism and the G₂ generators and relations. The G₂ graphical relations build on Kuperberg 1994; Morrison 2011 explicitly recalls this existing construction.
introductions.note: Credits the categorical spider construction, with the earlier graphical calculus recorded separately.

introductions.introduction_evidence: The paper establishes the non-elliptic G₂ web basis and its dimension comparison with invariant tensors. Morrison 2011 p. 190 identifies its Theorem 1.1 as imported from Kuperberg 1996.

The paper proves the combinatorial rank-two spiders agree with their algebraic representation-theoretic counterparts. Morrison 2011 p. 190 explicitly imports the G₂ braided-category equivalence as Theorem 1.2.

Theorem 7.5 includes the seven-dimensional irreducible U_q(G₂) module. Morrison 2011 abstract and Theorem 2.1 explicitly identify its main conclusion as Lehrer–Zhang’s prior theorem and supply another proof.
introductions.note: A specialized statement of the earlier result, not a new theorem introduced by the later paper.

introductions.introduction_evidence: The paper establishes braid generation for the strongly multiplicity-free quantum-group modules in its theorem, with proof in §8; the G₂ module is included explicitly.

The introduction answers the ENO cyclotomicity question negatively using the principal Haagerup and extended Haagerup fusion categories; this is a new conclusion, rather than a restated background theorem.
The paper announces and proves all four field-of-definition assertions as its main classification result in §§3–5.
The paper computes the Galois closures and classifies the resulting Haagerup and extended Haagerup Galois conjugates; these computations are among its announced new results.

judgments.reason: Reviewed §§1–3 and the computational appendix: the enduring theorem is explicitly credited to Lehrer–Zhang; spiders, webs and their basis/equivalence are credited to Kuperberg. The contribution is another proof. No additional reusable concept or new theorem is identified under the catalogue policy.
